thread:
perf-bot: nightly dashboard alert — region: us-west-2. Throughput down 14.8% vs 7d baseline, p50 latency +220ms, p95 +1.1s. Affected models: gpt-small-2.1 (cpu fallback spikes).

eli: saw the bot. did we roll anything to prod last night?
maria: yep merged PR 3421 at 00:12 UTC — kernel-selector heuristic change + fallback ordering tweak. It changed preference for CUTLASS->Eigen on certain matmul shapes.
sam: ci-bot flagged a perf test failure on that PR but merge pipeline was green after a flake. CI log: "perf/inference/throughput: -13%" (short window) — didn't block.

neha: quick sanity: is KV cache warmup different? dashboard shows cache hit-rate dip ~08:00-09:00 UTC aligning with the merge window. could be related.
maria: KV cache code wasn't touched in 3421, but kernel ordering could change latency which affects how often cache entries are used (racey TTL eviction).

eli: can we reproduce locally? sam, can you paste the perf test command you used?
sam: sure — run on a 16xA100 test node: 
```bash
python perf_run.py --model gpt-small-2.1 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --duration 300 --profile flame
```
Get p50/p95 and compare to baseline.

neha: i ran that in staging and saw p50 +180ms. profile attached (flamegraph link in the CI log). main hotspot is matmul kernel fallback path in op_x86.cc.
maria: that matches local pprof I grabbed: top stack shows `select_kernel()` returning alternate kernel for shapes [B=8, S=1024] due to a heuristic threshold change.

eli: do we have a quick bisect candidate range? commit range: a1b2c3..f7e8d9 (PR 3369..3421). 3421 is the obvious suspect. can someone bisect?
sam: starting git bisect now. i'll run the perf runner per-commit, but that will take ~4h. posting updates.

ci-bot: automated perf-check for commit f7e8d9 failed: throughput -12.7% (threshold -10%). See: https://ci.redwood/blue/organizations/..../results

neha: in parallel, i ported the heuristic change locally but force-pinned kernel ordering to pre-3421 to confirm. result: latency back to baseline. so it's almost surely the selector change.
maria: ok sounds like a revert for 3421 is reasonable as an immediate rollback. can we do a canary revert to dedicated pool first?

eli: yes — block full rollout. action items:
- sam: finish bisect and confirm minimal repro commit id (if not 3421 exactly).
- maria: open emergency revert PR pinned to main and start canary in us-west-2 dedicated pool. tag: @oncall-runtime.
- neha: prepare flamegraph + pprof excerpts and highlight select_kernel codepaths. attach to PR.
- ci-bot: run gated perf tests on revert PR (must pass perf threshold).

sam: bisect quick update: suspect commit f2d3e4 (sub-change inside 3421). when I checkout f2d3e4 performance regresses; when I revert only that file, perf recovered locally. posting exact commit in 15m.
maria: thanks — I'll draft the revert for that file (kernel_selector.cc) only. smaller blast radius.

eli: also note that the batching heuristics scheduler saw a small increase in average batch size from 5.3 -> 6.1 overnight; could amplify perf delta. please include these stats in the revert PR so we remember to test with different batching profiles.
neha: added a small repro script for CI: `scripts/repro_kselector.sh` which runs 3 sequential runs w/ cold cache to catch warmup differences. include this in the PR.

sam: revert PR opened: #3447 — reverting kernel selection lines in kernel_selector.cc (commit hash revert: r-9c8b7). requesting urgent review. canary scheduled to run in 10m.
maria: starting canary now — will monitor dashboard.

perf-bot: canary results (10m): throughput diff vs baseline +0.5%, p50 -12ms. Canary looks good.

eli: OK roll forward with revert to main and then create a follow-up PR to rework selector with better shape heuristics and unit perf tests.
maria: agreed. i'll coordinate postmortem and a checklist for future merges: include perf gate for kernel-selector changes, require perf regression run on same infra, and add a test for KV cache warmup effect.

neha: note for postmortem: we should add a synthetic test that exercises long-seq shapes (S>=768, batch 6-9) since those hit the fallback path.
sam: +1. also add a perf-smoke to merge pipeline that blocks on >8% throughput regressions.

eli: thanks everyone — great quick triage. leaving follow-ups in the revert PR. :thumbsup:
maria: merging revert to main once CI perf checks succeed.

ci-bot: revert PR #3447 perf-check: PASS. merging.

perf-bot: nightly alert resolved — metrics trending back to baseline in 30m window.

eli: file a short postmortem and include the reproducible command and flamegraphs. put it under /eng-runtime/postmortems.

maria: will do.
